findings.message: A different agent (Claude) checked the work in a separate headless process.

The parsing and reviewer-output validation are thorough and well tested. One error blocks approval: a proof's declared currency is never enforced. When a proof is `current_required`, both the checklist update path and the plan parser still accept `reusable_earlier_revision` evidence and mark the item complete. There are also no tests in this packet for the update path that writes to the plan file. The update path can report success while leaving a row the parser rejects, and it can move a completed item back to open.

Proof currency is declared but never enforced. Trigger: an item whose required proof has `currency: current_required` is updated with `evidenceClass: 'reusable_earlier_revision'` plus any non-empty `compatibilityReason`. `validateChecklistUpdate` only checks owner, proofId match and receipt fields, and `validateReceiptFields` only requires a compatibility reason for reusable evidence. Nothing compares the evidence class against `specification.currency`. `updatedChecklistContent` then writes `complete | reusable_earlier_revision | ...`, and `completeFieldsAreValid` accepts that row on every later parse. Result: an obligation the plan says needs current-revision proof is recorded as complete using earlier-revision evidence, which defeats the guarantee the `current_required` currency exists to give. Fix: in the update path, reject `reusable_earlier_revision` evidence for `current_required` proofs. In `parseDeliveryPlanContract`, apply the same check to completed items, and also require a `; compatible:` reason whenever the evidence class is `reusable_earlier_revision` (`isReceiptLocator` currently allows the reason to be missing).

No supplied test covers `updateDeliveryChecklistFile`, the only code here that writes `execution-plan.md`. None of the tests exercise its lock, its exact-snapshot compare-and-swap, its rewrite of only the mutable cells, the `proof_id_mismatch`/supporting-proof branch, or `compatible_reason_required`. Because of this, both the currency gap and the write defects below get through every named check. The write behaviour is unproven, and that is the shipped public wiring for recording delivery evidence.

`updateDeliveryChecklistFile` does not re-parse the content it writes, so some accepted inputs return `{ ok: true }` but leave a row the parser rejects. Examples: (a) `evidenceClass: 'partial_or_structural'` with a `compatibilityReason` writes `open | ... | receipt:x; compatible:y`, and `openFieldsAreValid` rejects any open row containing `; compatible:`. (b) A `receiptId` containing whitespace or `;` passes `validateReceiptFields` (it only checks `trim() !== ''`), but `isReceiptLocator` rejects it. (c) A `receiptId` ending in a backslash escapes the closing cell pipe and breaks the row. In each case, every later `parseDeliveryPlanContract` call fails until someone fixes the plan by hand. Suggested fix: run `parseDeliveryPlanContract` on `updated` before the rename, and apply the same identifier rules as `isReceiptLocator`.

An item can regress from complete to open. If `input.proofId` equals the item's real-boundary `requiredProof` but `evidenceClass` is `partial_or_structural`, the supporting-proof guard is skipped (it only runs when the proofIds differ). `updatedChecklistContent` then overwrites a `complete` row with `open | partial_or_structural`. Partial evidence should not be recorded against a real-boundary proof, and it should never downgrade a completed item.

`validateExecutionPlanOutput` compares the delivery definition and plan digest against trusted values only when `expectedDefinition` and `expectedNormalizedPlanDigest` are supplied. `runCandidate` passes `packet.execution_plan_delivery_definition` and `packet.execution_plan_normalized_digest`, which may be undefined (the runtime test packet omits both). In that case a reviewer-invented definition is approved after structural checks alone. Those checks also skip the 'testing needs a contributor real-boundary command proof' rule that `parseDeliveryPlanContract` enforces. Consider treating a missing trusted definition or digest as invalid for plan-execution packets.

A stale `.delivery-lock` left by a crash makes every later update return `delivery_update_pending` until someone deletes the lock by hand. The code comment acknowledges this, but nothing tells the user how to recover.
